meta.title: The Atlas — the pipeline as one map
meta.authored: hand-authored (ch12/ch13 precedent); LaTeX transcribed from code, derivations and paper/method.tex; history from CHANGELOG + [PHYSICS] commit log + docs/gates/G7_systematics_budget.md
meta.note: Node ids are stable deep-link anchors (atlas.html#node-id).

nodes.name: EMRI population model (M1)
nodes.hover: Where events come from: a piecewise EMRI rate over massive-black-hole mass, sampled in (M, z).
nodes.body: Every simulated detection starts as a draw from the Babak et al. (2017) M1 population: an EMRI rate per central black hole, piecewise in mass, sampled jointly in mass and redshift with an MCMC sampler.

variables.meaning: EMRI rate per massive black hole

refs: Babak et al. (2017), arXiv:1703.09722 — model M1

history.text: Population deepened to z = 1.5 — after the dt² inner-product fix the EMRI horizon reaches z ≈ 1.5, so the old z ≤ 0.5 depth was stale.
MCMC mixing strengthened (50 walkers, 10× longer burn-in) after campaign #51 diagnosed seed-dependent drift in the (M, z) chain.

chapter.label: Ch. 9 — Building a Universe to Break Your Estimator

nodes.name: Host-galaxy assignment
nodes.hover: Each sampled event is snapped to a real GLADE+ galaxy, which fixes its sky position and true redshift.
nodes.body: The sampled (M, z) event is resolved to an actual host in the GLADE+ galaxy catalogue (ball-tree lookup). The host fixes sky position, true redshift, and — through the mass relation — the black-hole mass the catalogue would predict.

variables.meaning: ecliptic sky position of the host

history.text: Hosts now use CMB-frame redshift z_cmb, not heliocentric — the frame the cosmology actually lives in.

chapter.label: Ch. 3 — Which Galaxy?

nodes.name: EMRI waveform + LISA response
nodes.hover: A 14-parameter AAK waveform, pushed through the full time-delay-interferometry response of LISA.
nodes.body: The event becomes a strain signal: an augmented-analytic-kludge EMRI waveform in 14 parameters (masses, spin, orbit, angles, distance, phases), passed through the TDI response that turns strain into the A and E data channels LISA actually records.
refs: Colpi et al. (2024), arXiv:2402.07571 — LISA definition study

history.text: Plunge-window initial conditions + official mission duration T = 4.5 yr (superseding an unofficial hardcoded 5 yr).

chapter.label: Ch. 6 — Opening the Black Box

nodes.name: LISA noise model Sₙ(f)
nodes.hover: What LISA cannot hear: instrumental noise (optical metrology + test masses) plus the galactic foreground.
nodes.body: The denominator of every inner product. Two instrumental terms — optical-metrology noise and test-mass acceleration noise — are combined through the TDI transfer function, and the unresolved galactic white-dwarf foreground is added on top.
nodes.latex: S_n^{A}(f) = \cls{tdi}{8\sin^2\!\Big(\tfrac{2\pi f L}{c}\Big)}\Big[\cls{oms}{S_{\rm OMS}(f)}\Big(\cos\tfrac{2\pi fL}{c}+2\Big)+2\Big(3+2\cos\tfrac{2\pi fL}{c}+\cos\tfrac{4\pi fL}{c}\Big)\cls{tm}{S_{\rm TM}(f)}\Big]+\cls{conf}{S_c^{A}(f)}

tdi.label: TDI transfer
tdi.note: The time-delay-interferometry combination imprints this sinusoidal transfer on all single-link noises.

oms.label: S_OMS — optical metrology
oms.note: (15 pm)² (1+(2 mHz/f)⁴)(2πf/c)² — displacement noise of the laser metrology chain.

tm.label: S_TM — test-mass acceleration
tm.note: (3 fm s⁻²)² (1+(0.4 mHz/f)²)(1+(f/8 mHz)⁴)(2πfc)⁻² — residual force noise on the free-falling test masses; dominates at low f.

conf.label: galactic confusion S_c^A
conf.note: Unresolved white-dwarf binaries in the Milky Way — a hump near a few mHz. Click to explore this term.

refs: Babak et al. (2023), arXiv:2303.15929 — LISA sensitivity

curve.title: A-channel PSD, with and without the galactic foreground

chapter.label: Ch. 6 — Opening the Black Box

nodes.name: Galactic confusion noise
nodes.hover: Millions of unresolved galactic white-dwarf binaries form a foreground hump in the mHz band.
nodes.body: The Milky Way's unresolved white-dwarf binaries add a stochastic foreground. Its knee frequency grows with observation time (more binaries get individually resolved and subtracted). It enters the A channel through the same TDI transfer as any stochastic strain background.
nodes.latex: S_c(f) = A f^{-7/3} e^{-(f/f_1)^{\alpha}}\cdot\tfrac12\Big[1+\tanh\Big(\tfrac{f_k-f}{f_2}\Big)\Big], \qquad \cls{transfer}{S_c^{A}(f) = \tfrac32\,(2x\sin x)^2\, S_c(f)},\;\; x=\tfrac{2\pi f L}{c}

transfer.label: TDI-A stochastic transfer
transfer.note: The raw strain-fit S_c must be pushed through the TDI response before it may be added to the instrumental TDI PSD — forgetting this overweighted the foreground by ~10⁶ near 0.2 mHz.

variables.meaning: foreground fit coefficients; f_1, f_k scale with observation time

history.text: Confusion noise added to the A/E PSD — previously absent entirely (known-bug #5).

TDI transfer applied to the confusion term: S_c^A = 1.5·(2x sin x)²·S_c. The raw strain fit had been added directly to the TDI PSD, overweighting the foreground by ~10⁶ near 0.2 mHz (campaign-51 high-M audit, item 4).

curve.title: Confusion hump inside the A-channel PSD

chapter.label: Ch. 6 — Opening the Black Box

nodes.name: Noise-weighted inner product
nodes.hover: The single most important operation in pipeline 1: how similar are two signals, given what LISA can hear?
nodes.body: Everything downstream — SNR, Fisher matrix, Cramér–Rao bounds — is built from this one operation: a frequency-domain overlap of two signals, weighted by the noise. It is also the pipeline's computational bottleneck.

dt2.label: Δt² — DFT normalization
dt2.note: The discrete Fourier transform's normalization. Its absence was the single largest defect ever found in this pipeline: SNR undercounted 10×, the population horizon shrank from z ≈ 1.5 to z ≈ 0.11. Toggle the history layer to see it.

spec.label: cross-spectrum
spec.note: Overlap of the two signals' Fourier transforms, channel by channel (A and E; the T null channel is excluded).

noise.label: noise weighting 1/Sₙ
noise.note: Frequencies where LISA is deaf contribute nothing. Click to explore the noise model.

history.text: G8 convention-pinning test written first — it exposed the missing Δt² factor.

Missing Δt² DFT normalization restored. SNR had been undercounted 10×, Cramér–Rao σ overcounted 10×, and the detectable population reached only z ≤ 0.11 instead of ≈ 1.5. G7 systematics-budget row #1 — the largest single systematic ever in the budget.

chapter.label: Ch. 6 — the dt² story is told here

nodes.name: Signal-to-noise ratio
nodes.hover: How loud is the event? The inner product of the signal with itself, square-rooted.
nodes.body: The optimal matched-filter SNR. It decides — at the gate to the right — whether an event counts as detected at all, and later (via the injection pool) it shapes the selection function p_det of the whole analysis.

history.text: Quick-SNR pre-screen disabled after a smoke audit measured a 0.55 % false-negative rate in the 1-yr pre-check.

chapter.label: Ch. 4 — The Universe Only Shows You Its Loud Half

nodes.name: Detection gate
nodes.hover: The threshold. Below SNR 20 an event is never seen — and that censoring is itself physics the inference must undo.
nodes.body: Only events with SNR ≥ 20 pass on to parameter estimation. This gate is not a technicality: it is the Malmquist selection that the inference pipeline must explicitly correct for, or H₀ comes out biased. The gate's shadow is the p_det node in the shared band below.

chapter.label: Ch. 4 — selection effects

nodes.name: Five-point stencil derivatives
nodes.hover: Numerical waveform derivatives, accurate to O(ε⁴) — the raw material of the Fisher matrix.
nodes.body: The Fisher matrix needs ∂h/∂θ for each of the 14 parameters. A five-point central stencil replaces the original O(ε) forward difference — four waveform evaluations per parameter, but errors fall as ε⁴ instead of ε.

s1.label: central 5-point combination
s1.note: The (−1, 8, −8, 1)/12 weights cancel error terms up to O(ε⁴) — see the error-scaling plot in the sidebar.

variables.origin: constant (~3×10⁻⁴ × scale, Vallisneri Eq. A11; M uses an absolute 1 M_\odot step)

history.text: Five-point stencil wired into the Fisher matrix as default, replacing the O(ε) forward difference (known-bug #4, HIGH).

curve.title: Derivative error vs step size: forward difference vs 5-point stencil

chapter.label: Ch. 6 — Opening the Black Box

nodes.name: Fisher matrix → Cramér–Rao
nodes.hover: The 14×14 information matrix; its inverse bounds how well each parameter can be measured.
nodes.body: Derivatives meet the inner product: the Fisher information matrix. Its inverse is the Cramér–Rao bound — the best possible covariance of any unbiased estimator. The (φ_S, θ_S, d_L) and mass sub-blocks of Σ are what pipeline 2 consumes as the GW measurement.

cov.label: Cramér–Rao covariance
cov.note: The inverse Fisher matrix — the forecast measurement covariance handed to the inference pipeline as a CSV.

history.text: G10 condition-number gate κ ≤ 10¹⁴ enforced — ill-conditioned matrices had fewer than 2 significant digits after inversion and are now skipped instead of stored as noise.

chapter.label: Ch. 6 — Opening the Black Box

nodes.name: Per-event Cramér–Rao CSV
nodes.hover: The handoff artifact: one row per detected event — parameters, SNR, and forecast covariances. Where pipeline 1 ends and pipeline 2 begins.
nodes.body: The two pipelines meet in a file. Pipeline 1 (GPU cluster) writes one CSV row per detected event: true parameters, SNR, and the Cramér–Rao covariance entries. Pipeline 2 (CPU) reads exactly this — it never sees a waveform.

variables.meaning: per-event covariance (3×3 sky+distance block; 4×4 with detector-frame mass)

nodes.impl: written by parameter_estimation.py, read by bayesian_statistics.py

chapter.label: Ch. 11 — the per-event dossier

nodes.name: Luminosity distance d_L(z, h)
nodes.hover: The one formula both pipelines share — and the only place H₀ enters the whole problem.
nodes.body: Flat ΛCDM luminosity distance, in closed hypergeometric form with a spline fast path. Pipeline 1 uses it to place hosts; pipeline 2 inverts it, asking for every candidate host: which H₀ would make this galaxy's redshift consistent with the measured distance? This is the entire H₀ sensitivity of the method, concentrated in one function.

dl.label: luminosity distance
dl.note: What a gravitational wave measures directly — no distance ladder, no calibration. The 'standard siren' property.

h0.label: H₀ — the target
h0.note: The only place the Hubble constant enters. Every posterior in this project is, at bottom, a statement about this denominator.

ez.label: expansion history E(z)
ez.note: Flat ΛCDM with Ω_m = 0.2726 (deliberately matched to the Barausse 2012 population, G11). wCDM (w₀, w_a) deliberately raises NotImplementedError rather than silently returning ΛCDM.

variables.meaning: H₀/(100 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹) — the inferred quantity

history.text: Spline-table fast path added — the hypergeometric evaluation was 52 % of the H₀-evaluation CPU time.
G11: fiducial Ω_m moved 0.25 → 0.2726, deliberately matched to the Barausse (2012) M1 population cosmology; the Planck-2018 mismatch is a tracked systematic (G7 row #6), not a bug.

caveats.text: wCDM (w₀ ≠ −1, w_a ≠ 0) is a guarded NotImplementedError — analytic distance is ΛCDM-only (GitHub #4).

curve.title: d_L(z) for h = 0.60 … 0.86 — the lever arm of the whole measurement

chapter.label: Ch. 1 — A Ruler That Needs No Ladder

nodes.name: Comoving volume element
nodes.hover: How much universe sits at each redshift — the population prior hiding inside every completion and kernel term.
nodes.body: The comoving volume per redshift slice. It weights the completion term (where could the unseen hosts be?) and — since the C7 kernel work — deconvolves the host-redshift prior itself.
refs: Gray et al. (2020), arXiv:1908.06050, App. A.2.3

chapter.label: Ch. 5 — The Galaxy You Cannot See

nodes.name: Detection probability p_det
nodes.hover: The gate's shadow: from thousands of injections, the probability that an event at distance d_L would have been detected.
nodes.body: The selection function, estimated empirically from the injection campaign: each injection's detection horizon is scaled from its SNR, and p_det(d_L) is the survival fraction of horizons beyond d_L. Optionally resolved in z and detector-frame mass for the mass channel.
nodes.latex: d_{{\rm hor},k} = \frac{\varrho_k\, d_{L,k}}{\varrho_{\rm thr}}, \qquad \cls{surv}{p_{\rm det}(d_L) = P\big(d_{\rm hor} \ge d_L\big)}

surv.label: survival estimator
surv.note: An empirical survival function over the injection pool's detection horizons — this replaced two earlier generations of kernel-regression estimators (see history).

history.text: F1: h-stable d_L bin edges for the histogram estimator.
F4: Nadaraya–Watson kernel estimator closed two spike mechanisms.
F4-v2: local-linear estimator fixed the d_L → 0 boundary bias.
Detection-horizon survival function replaced kernel regression entirely — the current estimator.
z-resolved survival S(d_L | z) (E1 FIX-2, flag-gated).
Joint z × M_z-resolved with-BH-mass selection survival (FIX-3 §7.1, default off).

curve.title: Smooth Malmquist p_det(d_L) — the calibration harness's toy form

chapter.label: Ch. 4 — The Universe Only Shows You Its Loud Half

nodes.name: Candidate-host query
nodes.hover: Which galaxies could have hosted this event? A ball-tree query of the 3σ localization volume.
nodes.body: For each detected event, the GLADE+ catalogue is queried for every galaxy inside the 3σ sky-and-distance localization volume implied by the event's Cramér–Rao covariance. These candidates are the sum over j in the likelihood.

chapter.label: Ch. 3 — Which Galaxy?

nodes.name: Host-redshift kernel p_g(z)
nodes.hover: What does a photo-z really tell you? A Gaussian is not enough — the volume prior must be deconvolved.
nodes.body: Each candidate's catalogued redshift carries photometric error (σ_z ≈ 0.035 for most of GLADE+) plus peculiar-velocity scatter. Treating that as a bare Gaussian silently applies an Eddington-type bias; the production kernel deconvolves the comoving-volume population prior.

pg.label: host-z kernel
pg.note: The prior a single catalogued galaxy puts on its own true redshift.

gauss.label: catalogue likelihood
gauss.note: Photometric redshift error plus peculiar-velocity scatter σ_z,pv = (1+z_g)·σ_v/c, added in quadrature — counted exactly once.

wpop.label: volume deconvolution
wpop.note: The population prior: more universe at higher z means a noisy photo-z more likely scattered down than up. Omitting this term was G7 row #2 (−2.4 % MAP bias at σ_z = 0.035).

history.text: Residual host peculiar velocity marginalized into the kernel (issue #16).
PV dispersion counted exactly once, per peculiar-velocity-correction class.
volume_trunc kernel variant implemented and empirically rejected — a seed-600 A/B showed it worsens the shallow bias.
C7-core: the volume-deconvolved kernel gains the catalogued-host selection intensity f_k·w_pop — physics-gate ledger entry, one of the two rows since the ledger opened.

caveats.text: At GLADE+ photo-z scatter σ_z ≈ 0.035 the bare-Gaussian kernel collapses P–P coverage to ~0–3 % — the volume kernel is the production default.

curve.title: Bare Gaussian vs volume-deconvolved kernel (z_g = 0.40, σ_z = 0.035)

chapter.label: Ch. 7 — A Redshift Is Not a Number

nodes.name: Stellar-mass → BH-mass relation
nodes.hover: The second handle: a galaxy's stellar mass predicts its central black-hole mass — with honest 0.24 dex scatter.
nodes.body: The mass channel's catalogue prior: the Reines & Volonteri (2015) AGN scaling from host stellar mass to central black-hole mass. The GW side measures the detector-frame mass superbly; the relation's intrinsic scatter is what limits the channel.

alpha.label: intercept α
alpha.note: 7.45 ± 0.08 — calibrated on the AGN sample of Reines & Volonteri (2015), Eq. (5).

scatter.label: intrinsic scatter
scatter.note: 0.24 dex — the dominant uncertainty of the predicted M_BH. It was entirely omitted before commit 555f018, and a precedence bug understated the stellar-mass term's variance ~100×.

history.text: Error budget repaired: the 0.24 dex intrinsic scatter had been omitted entirely, and an operator-precedence bug (a stray /10) understated the stellar-mass variance term ~100× — host-mass priors were 3–7× too tight.

curve.title: The relation with its ±0.24 dex intrinsic-scatter band

chapter.label: Ch. 8 — A Second Handle: the Mass Channel

nodes.name: Catalogue likelihood (standard channel)
nodes.hover: The heart of pipeline 2: sum over candidate hosts, marginalize over redshift, ask which H₀ fits.
nodes.body: The single-event likelihood over catalogued hosts. For each candidate, the GW 3D Gaussian (sky × distance, from the Cramér–Rao covariance) is evaluated at the distance that H₀ would assign to the host's redshift — then summed over candidates and normalized by the selection denominator, following Gray et al. (2020) Eq. A.10.
nodes.latex: L_{\rm cat}(H_0) = \frac{\sum_j \int dz\; \cls{pgw}{p_{\rm GW}\big(\phi_j, \theta_j,\, \cls{dlh}{d_L(z, H_0)}\big)}\; \cls{pgz}{p_g^{(j)}(z)}}{\cls{den}{\sum_j \int dz\; p_{\rm det}(z)\; p_g^{(j)}(z)}}

pgw.label: GW measurement
pgw.note: 3D Gaussian in (sky, distance) from the event's Cramér–Rao covariance — the entire output of pipeline 1, evaluated per host.

dlh.label: d_L(z, H₀) — the H₀ lever
dlh.note: The only H₀ dependence: each trial H₀ moves every host's predicted distance through the shared d_L(z, h) relation.

pgz.label: host-z kernel
pgz.note: The volume-deconvolved redshift prior of candidate j.

den.label: selection denominator
den.note: p_det appears in the denominator only (Mandel, Farr & Gair 2019) — putting it in the numerator double-counts selection. The normalization-mode saga (see history) lives here.

refs: Gray et al. (2020), arXiv:1908.06050, Eqs. A.9–A.10

history.text: Likelihood restructured to the single Gray ratio (partition-normalization fix).
Aligned with Gray Eq. A.9/A.10: ratio of sums, p_det in the denominator only.
In-catalogue H₀ normalization de-railed via explicit normalization_mode.
Default normalization flipped to volume_deconv; 'global' now warns (G7 row #5: the −17 % h-shape tilt of Option-A cancellation).
generator_marginal: generator-consistent selection normalization (E1 FIX-3).

chapter.label: Ch. 3 — Which Galaxy?

nodes.name: Mass-channel likelihood
nodes.hover: The 4D variant: add the superbly-measured detector-frame BH mass and let the catalogue's mass prediction vote on the host.
nodes.body: The with-BH-mass channel extends the GW Gaussian to 4D (sky, distance, detector-frame mass M_z = M_BH(1+z)) and marginalizes the unknown true BH mass analytically against the catalogue's Reines–Volonteri prediction — a conditional-Gaussian identity, so no extra numerical integral.
nodes.latex: \int\! dM_{\rm BH}\; p_{\rm GW}\big(\mathbf x,\, \cls{mz}{M_z}\big)\, \cls{gm}{g(M_{\rm BH})} = p_{\rm GW}^{(3)}(\mathbf x)\;\cls{cond}{\mathcal N\big(\mu_{\rm cond};\, \tilde\mu_g,\, \sigma_{\rm cond}^2 + \tilde\sigma_g^2\big)}

mz.label: detector-frame mass
mz.note: M_z = M_BH(1+z), measured from the waveform phasing to relative precision ~10⁻⁶ — the best-measured quantity in the problem.

gm.label: catalogue mass prior
gm.note: Gaussian from the Reines–Volonteri relation, with the honest 0.24 dex scatter.

cond.label: conditional-Gaussian closure
cond.note: Bishop (2006) Eq. 2.81–2.82: the mass marginalization collapses to a 1D Gaussian overlap — analytic, fast, exact.

variables.meaning: catalogue prior on true BH mass

history.text: mass_trunc host-mass kernel (EXP-45) implemented — then exonerated as the 2D bias driver.
2D truncated-lognormal mass kernel + host_mass_kernel flag ratified (#40 remainder).
G2d: Eddington-in-M host-mass rate prior, exact moment-matched.

caveats.text: G7 row #9: the mass marginal is not volume/rate-deconvolved the way the z-channel now is (Eddington-in-M) — unquantified, second-order, quoted as a paper caveat.

chapter.label: Ch. 8 — A Second Handle: the Mass Channel

nodes.name: Completion term
nodes.hover: The galaxies GLADE+ cannot see still host events — a uniform-in-comoving-volume term stands in for them.
nodes.body: GLADE+ is incomplete, badly so at EMRI distances. For the missing galaxies, the likelihood integrates the GW measurement against a uniform-in-comoving-volume population with (1+z)⁻¹ time dilation, following Gray et al. (2020) Eq. 32.
nodes.latex: L_{\rm comp}(H_0) = \frac{\int dz\; \cls{pgwz}{p_{\rm GW}(z)}\; \cls{volz}{\tfrac{dV_c}{dz}\tfrac{1}{1+z}}}{\int dz\; p_{\rm det}(z)\; \tfrac{dV_c}{dz}\tfrac{1}{1+z}}

pgwz.label: GW measurement at z
pgwz.note: The event's 3D density, sky-marginalized over the isotropic prior — evaluating it at a single peak-density sky point once inflated this term ~5000× (G7 row #3, fixed).

volz.label: volume × time dilation
volz.note: Uniform-in-comoving-volume host prior with (1+z)⁻¹ observer-clock dilation — the dilation factor was missing until commit 084db78.

variables.meaning: completeness fraction (weight between L_cat and L_comp)

history.text: Spurious p_det removed from the completion-term numerator (Gray Eq. 32).
(1+z)⁻¹ time dilation added to the completion integrals.
Completion numerator sky-marginalized over the isotropic 1/(4π) prior — the peak-density shortcut had inflated it ~5000× (G7 row #3).
Solid-angle Jacobian sin θ + z ≥ 0 window clamp (G7 row #4).
Completion numerator capped at the analysis-depth limit.

chapter.label: Ch. 5 — The Galaxy You Cannot See

nodes.name: Completeness mixture
nodes.hover: The two worlds — catalogued and dark — weighted by how complete the catalogue actually is at that distance.
nodes.body: The per-event likelihood is a mixture: the catalogue term weighted by the completeness fraction f_i (from a per-pixel Schechter-function threshold map), plus the completion term weighted by 1 − f_i.

fi.label: completeness fraction
fi.note: Per-pixel Schechter apparent-magnitude threshold m_th over a HEALPix map — how much of the luminosity function GLADE+ actually catches there.

fi2.label: completeness fraction
fi2.note: Same f_i — what the catalogue misses goes to the completion term.

variables.meaning: catalogue completeness at the event's sky pixel and inferred z

history.text: Per-pixel Schechter completeness (PixelCompleteness + m_th map).
astropy_healpix + apparent-B-magnitude parsing from GLADE+.
Sky-aware selection function — closed the isotropic-p_det sky blind spot (the paper-blocking finding of the inference-consistency audit).

chapter.label: Ch. 5 — The Galaxy You Cannot See

nodes.name: Selection normalization D(h)
nodes.hover: The global denominator that undoes Malmquist bias — and the site of the pipeline's longest-running battle.
nodes.body: The normalization that makes the likelihood a proper density over detectable data (Gray et al. A.19). Getting its h-dependence wrong tilts the whole posterior; this node has the densest scar tissue on the map, including the 2026-08 one-detection-model unification.
nodes.latex: D(h) = \iint \cls{sel}{p_{\rm det}}\; p_{\rm pop}(z, M \mid h)\; dz\, dM \qquad \text{(evaluated by deterministic Gauss–Legendre quadrature)}

sel.label: selection function
sel.note: The same p_det as everywhere else — since path-A C9+C8 (2026-08-04) a single detection model S̄_φ is used consistently across mixture and completion mass density.

variables.meaning: phase-marginal survival — the one detection model

refs: Gray et al. (2020), arXiv:1908.06050, Eq. A.19

history.text: Diagnostic normalization_mode='volume_global' for the G3 ablation cube.
Partition-norm denominators precomputed (β_G, global catalogue selection; verified no-op).
Monte-Carlo selection denominator replaced by deterministic 2D Gauss–Legendre quadrature — eliminated 1 % unseeded run-to-run noise (G7 row #10).
Path-A C9+C8: one detection model S̄_φ — mass-consistent mixture and completion mass density. Physics-gate ledger entry.

caveats.text: G7 row #5: the Option-A global cancellation (Σ_global vs h³β_G) produced a −17 % h-shape tilt — avoided via local modes; 'global' mode now warns.

chapter.label: Ch. 4 — selection, and its denominator

nodes.name: Log-space combination
nodes.hover: Forty quiet events beat one loud one: per-event likelihoods multiply — in log space, they add.
nodes.body: Independent events multiply; numerically, their log-likelihoods are summed on the h grid and exponentiated once (log-sum-exp). No extra β(h)^N factor appears — it cancels against the Poisson rate prior. Zero-likelihood handling strategies are explicit and audited.

history.text: Tier-3 audit removed the earlier −N·log D(h) outer correction — it over-applied the selection correction on top of the per-event denominators.

chapter.label: Ch. 2 — Bayes, Once and For All

nodes.name: The H₀ posterior
nodes.hover: The destination: a probability density over the Hubble constant, from gravity alone.
nodes.body: Everything on this map exists to shape this one curve: the posterior over h on a uniform prior [0.60, 0.86]. Its honest current state — including the residual bias story — is chapters 11–13.

ev.label: per-event likelihood
ev.note: The completeness mixture, one factor per detected EMRI.

variables.meaning: the galaxy catalogue (GLADE+) and everything known about it

history.text: Phase 48 production fine-grid sweep: h = 0.73 closure passed at 63-point resolution.

chapter.label: Ch. 11 — The State of the Art, Honestly

nodes.name: P–P calibration harness
nodes.hover: Does the posterior mean what it claims? Synthetic universes with known H₀ test the estimator's coverage.
nodes.body: Not on the production path — above it. The validation harness builds synthetic universes with known h, runs the single-host estimator, and checks coverage: an x % credible interval must contain the truth x % of the time. This harness is where the bare-Gaussian kernel bias was caught and quantified.

variables.meaning: central credible interval of mass p

history.text: Catalogue / impostor-ball synthetic universe + production-stack analog.
mixture_mode='absolute' (Variant-1 harness analog).

chapter.label: Ch. 10 — Is It Calibrated?
